subject: Model fit eval — open models vs proprietary parity + next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Sanders <katie@paygrid.com>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + requested artifacts (prompt set / thresholds)

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up with: 

1) Summary of where we landed
- You'd like us to run a model-fit evaluation on your production prompt set (~12k samples from the ingestion pipeline) focused on summary quality and classification accuracy.
- Primary business requirement: match or come within an acceptable delta of your current proprietary baseline on end-user summary acceptance (you mentioned relevance/conciseness metrics).

2) What we'll deliver
- Preliminary benchmark CSV with per-model metrics (we'll include NDCG@5, semantic similarity, and classification F1).
- Prompt set export (you mentioned removing PII — please confirm).
- Recommendation slide with our suggested candidate models and a parity assessment.

3) Questions for you
- Final prompt set: please confirm the version you want evaluated (production export vs. redaction-needed).
- Acceptance thresholds: you mentioned “parity” — do you want absolute parity (within 1–2% of current baseline) or a minimum of 95% of baseline performance?
- Timeline: is a two-week turnaround okay for the initial eval?

I attached the Redwood recommendation slide (high level) and will follow up with the CSV once we run the small pilot run.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Katie Sanders <katie@paygrid.com>

Cc: Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + requested artifacts (prompt set / thresholds)

Thanks Lauren — nice demo.

- I've attached a redacted prompt export (paygrid-promptset-v2.jsonl). We've removed direct PII but left realistic context. Please do not share outside your eval team.
- On thresholds: our product metric is "user-accept" (binary), and the current proprietary baseline has an acceptance rate of 87% on this set. Ideally we want open models to be within 2 percentage points (>=85%) on that metric; if not, we need clear guidance on failure modes.
- Timeline: two weeks is fine for an initial pass. If you can include per-prompt failure examples that would help our PMs assess regressions quickly.

Look forward to the benchmark CSV.

—Katie
Katie Sanders | Head of Product, PayGrid
katie@paygrid.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Attachments: paygrid-promptset-v2.jsonl

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Sanders <katie@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + requested artifacts (prompt set / thresholds)

Hi Katie / team — thanks for the prompt set. We've run a small pilot (1k sample subset) and attaching the preliminary CSV with key metrics. High-level findings: 

- Models evaluated: OpenLlama-34B-QLoRA, Mistral-7B-Instruct (8-bit), and Redwood Proprietary v2 (baseline).
- Summary of results (pilot):
  • Redwood Proprietary v2: user-accept = 87.0% (baseline)
  • Mistral-7B-Instruct (instr-tuned): user-accept = 86.1% (within 1% absolute)
  • OpenLlama-34B-QLoRA (w/ prefix tuning): user-accept = 83.9%

Interpretation: Mistral-7B-Instruct matches closely on summary/conciseness and is within your 2-point threshold in this subset; OpenLlama-34B shows useful signal but is ~3.1 points below baseline on this pilot. Per-prompt error patterns (attached sample rows): OpenLlama tends to hallucinate numeric fields and truncate long-context summaries; Mistral shows occasional verbosity but higher faithfulness.

Recommended next steps (technical):
- Run full eval on the 12k prompt set (2 weeks) with NDCG@5, semantic-similarity (USE/Cohere-style embedding sim), and per-prompt diff examples flagged when acceptance flips from baseline.
- For any candidate open model within ~2.5 absolute points, we recommend a targeted prompt-template iteration + light RLHF/LLM-tuning (few-shot + prefix tuning) before deeming it non-viable.
- Quantization note: Mistral 7B inference at 8-bit retains performance and will reduce cost by ~3–4x vs baseline; OpenLlama-34B QLoRA works but needs calibration on numeric extraction tasks.

I've attached: paygrid-open-vs-proprietary-benchmarks.csv (pilot), and flagged ~20 representative failure examples inline in the CSV.

Let us know if you want us to proceed with the full 12k run — we can start tomorrow and have results in ~10 business days.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao | Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Attachments: paygrid-open-vs-proprietary-benchmarks.csv

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Sanders <katie@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — open models vs proprietary parity + next steps

Appreciate the quick pilot and the CSV, Aditya — good signal. Katie — per your acceptance criteria, here's the alignment and proposed plan: 

Action items / agreement:
1) PayGrid confirms: proceed with full eval on the 12k redacted set (paygrid-promptset-v2.jsonl). Katie: please reply-all with a one-line confirmation that we have permission to run the full evaluation on the redacted export.
2) Acceptance threshold: PayGrid keeps the 2pp tolerance on user-accept (>=85% on our evaluation) for initial parity. If an open model is within this band, Redwood will run one round of prompt-template optimization and a light prefix-tuning pass to try and close the gap.
3) Timeline & deliverables:
   - Start: 2027-05-23 (on approval)
   - Full eval complete: ~2027-06-06 (10 business days)
   - Deliverables: full benchmark CSV, per-prompt failure examples, recommendation slide with cost delta and suggested rollout plan (canary + A/B test).
4) Next meeting: 2027-06-08 to review results and decide canary parameters.

If that looks good I'll mark this in HubSpot and get the eval job queued as soon as we have your confirmation.

—Lauren
